question: Should OpenClaw add a native child-session context-pressure notification contract, and what threshold, parent target, operator alert, and recovery semantics should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior adds new product/API/config semantics around agent hierarchy and recovery, and current source only proves the gap rather than a narrow mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define Narrow Core Contract
options.body: Specify a default or opt-in threshold, parent/requester resolution, operator notification surface, and non-destructive recovery behavior before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Watchdog Design
options.body: Treat this as one slice of the broader subagent stall and recovery design so context pressure, inactivity, and completion loss share one liveness contract.

options.title: Wait For Live Fleet Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until the reporter or maintainer captures a diagnostics export or replay proving the exact saturated-child failure mode on current main.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Core Contract
recommendation.body: Specify a default or opt-in threshold, parent/requester resolution, operator notification surface, and non-destructive recovery behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest local history across subagent cleanup/session semantics and are a reasonable owner for the product boundary decision.
